notes: Brackets are derived. The booklet prints no bracket schedule: it prints a Tax Table of 2,000 rows, 50 dollars wide, for taxable income under 100,000 (PDF pages 27-38), and on page 38 two worksheets for 100,000 or more: '$4,562 plus 0.0475 over $100,000' for single or married filing separate, and '$4,373 plus 0.0475 over $100,000' for married filing joint, head of household or qualified widow(er). The rates and starts were fitted to the table. Worked over all 2,000 rows at the row midpoint, the schedule differs from the printed figure by at most 0.44 dollars in both columns, so every row is the schedule's result rounded to the dollar. At 100,000 the schedule gives 4,561.50 (printed 4,562) and 4,373.00 (printed 4,373); at 200,000 it gives 9,311.50 against the worksheet's 9,312, and 9,123.00 against 9,123.

How tightly the table fixes the fit, changing one figure at a time and requiring every row to stay within 0.50 of its printed tax: the first start in each column can move by up to 12 dollars and each other start by up to 6, and no rate can move by 0.05 of a percentage point. Starts single 1,000, 2,500, 3,750, 4,900, 7,200 and joint 2,000, 5,000, 7,500, 9,800, 14,400 are the round figures inside those ranges. The second column's starts are exactly double the first's.

The worksheets are not in brackets.derivation.formula: that field holds one 'rate x income minus constant' tested against both columns, the two columns have different constants, and their constants as 'minus' figures (188 and 377) are not printed. The printed 'Tax on $100,000' figures are table rows at income 100000, so the validator re-checks both columns and the two other statuses at the worksheet's starting point. The worksheet rate 0.0475 is the top bracket rate.

The table's columns are 'Single or married filing separate' and 'Married* filing joint or head of household'; the footnote reads 'This column must also be used by a Qualified Surviving Spouse.' So married_separate copies the first column and head_of_household the second; qualifying surviving spouse has no key in brackets and uses the joint list. Table rows are recorded for all four keys so the validator checks each list.
Docling reads the 85,400-85,450 row's joint tax as 3,683; the pypdf text reads 3,681 and the schedule gives 3,680.69. The pypdf figure is used.

Social Security: PDF page 16: 'Social Security benefits that are included in the Federal AGI shall be subtracted.' PDF page 45, Schedule 511-A line 2 'Social Security benefits taxed on your Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR'. The Help Center page says the same. Recorded as exempt.

Resident income: PDF page 3: 'An Oklahoma resident individual is taxed on all income reported on the federal return, except income from real and tangible personal property located in another state, income from business activities in another state, or the gains/losses from the sales or exchange of real property in another state.' PDF page 9 says line 4 out-of-state income 'is not non-business interest or dividends, installment sale interest, salary/wages, pensions, unemployment compensation, gambling, or income from personal services.' So a pension stays in Oklahoma income unless a Schedule 511-A line takes it out.

Lines 5 and 6 of Schedule 511-A share one 10,000 limit per person: PDF page 17: 'the amount of the exclusion on this line cannot exceed $10,000 minus the amounts already claimed on Schedule 511-A, line 5 (if less than zero, enter "0")'. Each line also stops at the amount included in Federal AGI. The booklet prints no age test on either line. Line 5 adds 'To be eligible, you must have retirement income in your name'; line 6 says only 'Each individual'.

Another state's government pension, New York State included: no sentence in the booklet or the Help Center page names one, and New York appears in neither. Line 5 is a closed list ('The retirement benefits must be received from the following') of the U.S. civil service and named Oklahoma systems, so a New York State pension is not on it. Line 6 is a list of plan types, not payers: 'The retirement benefits must be received from the following and satisfy the requirements of the IRC' (IRC Sec. 401, 457, 408, 403(a) or (b), 86, 402(e)). Whether a New York State pension reaches line 6 therefore turns on whether its plan is one of the listed types, and the booklet does not say which type any other state's plan is. public_pension_other_state is in covers_unclear on line 6 for that reason. If the plan is not a listed type, no line takes it out and it is taxed (PDF page 3).

Roth conversions: PDF page 20: 'Rollovers and IRA Conversions are taxed in the same year as on the federal return.' The booklet does not say whether a converted amount counts as retirement benefits on line 6, so roth_conversion is in covers_unclear. Separately, the age 65 exemption's Federal AGI limits leave conversion income out (PDF page 9).

Special (age 65) exemption: PDF page 9, an additional exemption 'for each taxpayer or spouse' who is 65 or older at the close of the tax year, on a single return with line 1 equal to 15,000 or less, joint 25,000 or less, married filing separate 12,500 or less, head of household 19,000 or less. '*Note: If your Federal AGI includes income from the conversion of a traditional individual retirement account to a Roth individual retirement account, this income shall be excluded in determining the Federal AGI limits. Provide a copy of your federal return and Form 8606.' The schema's measure has no field for this, so the measure is federal_agi with the exclusion in as_printed. The four numbered returns do not include a qualifying surviving spouse: no limit for that status is found in the booklet, and it does not say whether that filer may claim this exemption.
Age: PDF page 9: 'If you turned age 65 on January 1, 2026, you are considered to be age 65 at the end of 2025.'

Standard deduction: PDF page 10: 'If you claimed the standard deduction on your federal return, you must claim the Oklahoma standard deduction. If you claimed itemized deductions on your federal return, you must claim Oklahoma itemized deductions.' The filer has no choice of the larger. A person claimed as a dependent still gets the standard deduction but enters 0 for the regular exemption (PDF pages 8 and 10).

Oklahoma itemized deductions: Schedule 511-D starts from federal Schedule A, takes out state and local sales or income tax, and is limited to 17,000; 'Charitable contributions and medical expenses are not subject to the $17,000 limit' (PDF page 10; form PDF page 46). This is a limit on itemized deductions, not a deduction of 17,000, so it is here and not in base.deductions.

Exemptions: 'Oklahoma allows $1,000 for each exemption claimed on the top of the return' (PDF page 10; form line 11, PDF page 43). A spouse's exemption on a separate or head of household return requires that the spouse had no income, is not filing and cannot be claimed as a dependent (PDF page 8). The booklet prints no phase-out of the regular exemptions or the standard deduction.

Federal civil service: CSRS paid in lieu of Social Security is excluded 100% on line 3, apart from the 10,000 limit; FERS does not qualify except a CSRS component and the FERS Annuity Supplement (PDF page 17). Other U.S. civil service retirement is on line 5, without CSRS benefits already excluded on line 3. Military retirement (line 4) and Railroad Retirement (line 7) are separate and unlimited.

An early distribution due to termination of employment before retirement or disability (generally code 1 in box 7) does not qualify on line 5 but 'may qualify for the "Other Retirement Income" exclusion on Schedule 511-A, line 6' (PDF page 17).

Capital gain deduction: 'You can deduct qualifying gains receiving capital treatment that are included in Federal AGI' (PDF page 18). No percentage is printed; recorded as a deduction of the full qualifying gain (value 1), with the three tests in condition.

Interest on U.S. government obligations is subtracted on line 1; FNMA and GNMA interest does not qualify (PDF page 16). The active military pay exclusion is on Schedule 511-C line 1 (PDF pages 22 and 46); it is not retirement income.

Out-of-state income (Form 511 line 4) is real or tangible personal property or business income in another state; a filer with such income prorates deductions and exemptions on Schedule 511-E (PDF pages 9 and 25). Out-of-state losses are added back on Schedule 511-B line 2 (PDF page 20). Lump-sum distributions not in Federal AGI are added on Schedule 511-B line 3 and may qualify for a retirement exclusion (PDF page 20).

Credits are not recorded as entries: child care/child tax credit (PDF page 11), credit for tax paid to another state (page 11), Credit for Property Tax Relief for a person 65 or older or disabled with gross household income up to 12,000, at most 200 (page 14), Sales Tax Relief with an income limit raised to 50,000 at 65 or older (page 15), and the earned income credit at 5% of the federal credit. None depends on the kind of retirement income.

The booklet prints no surtax, no recapture of lower brackets and no statement on inflation indexing: not found in the booklet. The 10% additional tax on non-qualified Health Savings Account withdrawals (line 14b, PDF page 10) applies to those withdrawals, not to income over a threshold.

Settlement 2026-11-07: brackets.derivation.method: A said tax_table_and_formula, B said tax_table; PDF pages 27 and 38 print both a table and worksheets for 100,000 or more, so tax_table_and_formula, with no formula object because the constants differ by column.

Settlement 2026-11-07: brackets.derivation.table_rows: A listed 14 rows, B listed 14 other rows; all 28 are printed (checked against the table), and neither set reaches every band of both columns. Replaced by 26 rows that sit either side of each band edge in each column and include the page 38 figures at 100,000.

Settlement 2026-11-07: base.deductions itemized_cap: A left it out and B recorded it as a deduction of 17,000 per return; PDF page 10 says Oklahoma itemized deductions 'are limited to, and may not exceed, $17,000', a limit and not a deduction, so it is in notes and not in base.deductions.

Settlement 2026-11-07: capital_gains exempt_obligation_gains: A recorded it and B did not; PDF page 16 says 'The capital gain/loss from the sale of an U.S. Government obligation is exempt' and PDF page 20 says the same of Oklahoma obligations, with Schedule 511-A line 11 on page 18. Kept.

Settlement 2026-11-07: indexing: A gave all_other only, B added brackets and standard_deduction as not_stated; the booklet says nothing on either, and extraction brief rule 8 asks for an entry only where it does. A's single all_other entry kept.
